bib.title: Introduction to Information Retrieval, Chapter 21: Link analysis
bib.venue: Cambridge University Press (online edition, April 1, 2009 draft)

question: How can the hyperlink structure of the web (anchor text, PageRank, HITS) be used to score and rank web pages for search?
contributions: Anchor text as a description of the target page
PageRank as steady state of a random surfer with teleport
HITS hub and authority scores with root and base sets

results.claim: PageRank is query-independent static quality; search engines combine it with hundreds of features such as cosine similarity and term proximity in a machine-learned composite score.

limits: Chapter is textbook exposition; the only numbers are worked examples on 3- and 7-node graphs, plus a few unsourced rules of thumb (200-page root set, five iterations, ten out-links, alpha 0.1)
No evaluation of ranking quality from link analysis; relative weight of PageRank in the composite score is deferred to machine-learned scoring (Section 15.4.1)
Link spam and link farms are noted to affect both PageRank and HITS, no countermeasure given beyond discounting internal links and spam detection

Dated (2008): describes web search as of 2008 (dmoz open directory, Yahoo directory, Big Blue / evil empire anchor examples, machine-learned scoring without neural ranking); no mention of dense retrieval, or of graph signals in RAG
HITS and AA^T described as eigen-computation 'of a stochastic matrix' although AA^T is not stochastic

Inconsistencies: Example 21.1 and 21.2 text labels nodes q1.. while Fig 21.4 uses d0..d6 and score vectors are 0-indexed; PageRank said to be between 0 and 1 (s21.2) and in [0,1) for topic-specific; Example 21.1 PageRank entries sum to 1.01; alpha typical 0.1 vs example 0.14
practices: Discount internal (same-site, template) links when running link analysis (p.462, s21.1)
Index anchor text terms of in-links under the target page with a special indicator and weight by frequency with an idf-like penalty; learn weights with machine-learned scoring (p.463)
Use PageRank as one query-independent feature in a learned composite score, not as the ranking by itself (p.469)
Compute PageRank by power iteration until frequencies change by less than a threshold (p.468)
For personalised ranking, precompute topic-specific PageRanks and mix them linearly (p.473)
For HITS, build a root set of about 200 text-matching pages, expand to a base set with in- and out-neighbours, then run about five additive updates (p.477-478)
Use link analysis also to prioritise crawling (front queues of Chapter 20) (p.461)

terms.definition: a numerical score between 0 and 1 assigned to every node in the web graph, equal to the steady-state visit frequency of a random surfer with teleport
operation in which the surfer jumps from a node to any node in the web graph, chosen uniformly at random
there exists a positive integer T0 such that for all pairs of states i, j, if started in i then for all t > T0 the probability of being in state j at time t is greater than 0
PageRank computed with teleport restricted to a non-empty set S of pages on a topic
PageRank for a user interest mixture, expressed as a linear combination of topic-specific PageRanks
a good hub points to many good authorities; a good authority is pointed to by many good hubs; computed iteratively
Hyperlink-Induced Topic Search: principal eigenvectors of AA^T (hubs) and A^TA (authorities) over the base set
root set: pages containing the query terms; base set: root set plus pages linking to or linked from it
pages set up to point at a target to inflate its in-link count; link farms collude to raise scores under link analysis algorithms
